summary.en: Y Combinator, founded in March 2005 in San Francisco by Paul Graham, Jessica Livingston, Robert Morris and Trevor Blackwell, is the pioneering and most prestigious US seed accelerator. Its standard deal invests $500,000 ($125K for 7% on a post-money SAFE plus a $375K uncapped MFN SAFE) over a 12-week, four-batches-per-year program ending in Demo Day. It has funded more than 5,000 companies with a combined valuation around $600B, including Airbnb, Stripe, Dropbox, Coinbase, DoorDash, Reddit and Instacart.

summary.en: Techstars, founded in 2006 in Boulder, Colorado (now HQ'd in New York City) by David Cohen, Brad Feld, David Brown and Jared Polis, is a global mentor-driven accelerator network. As of its Fall 2025 terms it invests $220,000 ($20K for 5% common stock plus a $200K uncapped MFN SAFE) over a ~13-week program. It admits roughly 1-2% of applicants (~12 per cohort) and has backed 3,500+ companies including SendGrid, DigitalOcean, Uber, Chainalysis and Zipline, with portfolio market cap reported around $124B.

summary.en: Plug and Play Tech Center, founded in 2006 in Sunnyvale, California by Saeed Amidi, is an early-stage investor, accelerator and corporate innovation platform. It runs 60+ industry-focused accelerator batches across 35+ locations connecting startups with 550+ corporate partners; participation is generally equity-free, with optional PnP Ventures investment ($25K-$500K, ~1-5% equity). summary.en: AngelPad, founded in 2010 by ex-Google's Thomas Korte and Carine Magescas, is a highly selective, small-cohort accelerator operating from San Francisco and New York City. It invests $120,000 per company (~7% equity) plus $300K+ in cloud credits over an intensive ~3-month program with two cohorts per year of ~15 teams.
